units.zh: 泓曰：「懸爵於朝，所以懲勸來效，標明盛德。
units.en: Yao Hong replied: "Titles exist to reward future service and mark true virtue.
units.literal: Hong said, "Suspending rank in court is to punish and encourage coming merit and mark splendid virtue.

proposals.before: Yao Hong replied: "Titles exist to reward future service and mark true virtue.
proposals.after: Yao Hong replied, “The court holds out titles to admonish and encourage those who will render service and to give public recognition to outstanding virtue.
proposals.reason: 懲勸 expresses both admonition and encouragement of future service.

units.zh: 元子遭家不造，與宮臣同此百憂，獨享其福，得不愧於心乎！」
units.en: I share every grief with my household staff—how could I hoard favors for myself alone?"
units.literal: Yuanzi meets the house in misfortune, sharing every worry with palace officials—how could he alone enjoy the blessing without shame in heart!"

proposals.before: I share every grief with my household staff—how could I hoard favors for myself alone?"
proposals.after: I, Yuanzi, have seen my house struck by misfortune. My palace officers shared all these troubles with me. Could I enjoy the good fortune alone without feeling ashamed?”
proposals.reason: 遭家不造 specifies Hong’s family calamity, and Yuanzi is Hong’s self-designation.

units.zh: 贊默然。
units.en: Yao Zan held his tongue.
units.literal: Zan was silent.

units.zh: 姚紹進曰：「陛下不忘報德，封之是也，古者敬其事，命之以始，可須來春，然後議之。」
units.en: Yao Shao urged delay: "Reward them, yes, but wait until spring as the ancients would."
units.literal: Yao Shao advanced and said, "Your Majesty not forgetting to repay virtue—enfeoffing them is right; the ancients respected the affair and charged them with its beginning—it is possible to wait until next spring, then deliberate."

proposals.before: Yao Shao urged delay: "Reward them, yes, but wait until spring as the ancients would."
proposals.after: Yao Shao stepped forward. “Your Majesty remembers to reward virtue, and you are right to grant them fiefs. In antiquity people treated such matters with reverence, timing the appointments for the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then deliberate.”
proposals.reason: Restore Shao’s expressed approval of repaying virtue, the ancient practice of attending to the beginning, and his proposal to deliberate next spring.

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: Yao Hong dropped the plan.
units.literal: Thereupon he desisted.

value.action: was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as fifth-rank viscounts and barons, then desisted

units.zh: 并州、定陽、貳城胡數萬落叛泓，入於平陽，攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡，推匈奴曹弘為大單于，所在殘掠。
units.en: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
units.literal: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, pushed the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.

proposals.before: Tens of thousands of Hu households in Bing, Dingyang, and Ercheng rose against Yao Hong, entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, raised the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
proposals.after: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.
proposals.reason: 立義 is an abbreviated general’s title, and 落 counts tribal households or encampments, not tens of thousands of settlements.

proposals.before: Several tens of thousands of settlements of Hu in Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against Hong and entered Pingyang, attacked Liyi Yao Chengdu at the Xiongnu fort, pushed the Xiongnu Cao Hong as great shanyu, and wherever they went ravaged and plundered.
proposals.after: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.
proposals.reason: 立義 is an abbreviated general’s title, and 落 counts tribal households or encampments, not tens of thousands of settlements.

value.action: attacked at the Xiongnu fort by Hu rebels
pushed as great shanyu; ravaged widely; entered Pingyang
Hu of Bingzhou, Dingyang, and Ercheng rebelled against him

units.zh: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘，戰於平陽，大破之，執弘，送于長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。
units.en: Yao Yi marched from Puban, shattered them at Pingyang, sent Cao Hong to Chang'an, and resettled fifteen thousand elite households in Yongzhou.
units.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Cao Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.

proposals.before: Yao Yi marched from Puban, shattered them at Pingyang, sent Cao Hong to Chang'an, and resettled fifteen thousand elite households in Yongzhou.
proposals.after: Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East, marched from Puban against Cao Hong, routed him at Pingyang, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. Yi resettled fifteen thousand leading households in Yongzhou.
proposals.reason: Restore Yi’s title and the seizure of Cao Hong before he was sent away.

proposals.before: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi from Puban campaigned against Cao Hong, fought at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized Cao Hong, sent him to Chang'an, and moved fifteen thousand notable settlements to Yongzhou.
proposals.after: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi set out from Puban against Cao Hong. He fought at Pingyang, routed Hong, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. He transferred fifteen thousand of their leading households to Yongzhou.
proposals.reason: 落 counts households or tribal encampments here; the translation inflates their settlement count.

value.action: fought p029 at Pingyang, greatly defeated him, seized him, sent him to Chang'an, moved 15000 notable settlements to Yongzhou

units.zh: 仇池公楊盛攻陷祁山，執建節王總，遂逼秦州。
units.en: Yang Sheng of Chouqi seized Qishan, captured Wang Zong, and drove on Qinzhou.
units.literal: Duke of Chouqi Yang Sheng attacked and took Qishan, seized Jianjie Wang Zong, then pressed Qinzhou.

proposals.before: Yang Sheng of Chouqi seized Qishan, captured Wang Zong, and drove on Qinzhou.
proposals.after: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.
proposals.reason: 仇池 is Chouchi, and 建節 is Wang Zong’s military designation, not part of his name; preserve Sheng’s ducal rank.

proposals.before: Duke of Chouqi Yang Sheng attacked and took Qishan, seized Jianjie Wang Zong, then pressed Qinzhou.
proposals.after: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.
proposals.reason: 仇池 is Chouchi, and 建節 is Wang Zong’s military designation, not part of his name; preserve Sheng’s ducal rank.

units.zh: 泓遣後將軍姚平救之，盛引退。
units.en: Yao Hong sent Yao Ping; Yang Sheng pulled back.
units.literal: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to rescue him; Sheng withdrew.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Yao Ping; Yang Sheng pulled back.
proposals.after: Yao Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to relieve Qinzhou, and Yang Sheng withdrew.
proposals.reason: Restore Ping’s rank and mission to relieve Qinzhou.

units.zh: 姚嵩與平追盛及於竹嶺，姚贊率隴西太守姚秦都、略陽太守王煥以禁兵赴之。
units.en: Yao Song and Yao Ping chased Yang Sheng to Bamboo Ridge while Yao Zan brought Yao Qindu and Wang Huan with palace troops.
units.literal: Yao Song with Ping pursued Sheng as far as Bamboo Ridge; Yao Zan led Longxi Grand Administrator Yao Qindu and Lüeyang Grand Administrator Wang Huan with household troops to hurry there.

proposals.before: Yao Song and Yao Ping chased Yang Sheng to Bamboo Ridge while Yao Zan brought Yao Qindu and Wang Huan with palace troops.
proposals.after: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.
proposals.reason: 及 means actually catching up with Sheng, and the two 太守 are governors of the named commanderies; 禁兵 are palace guards.

proposals.before: Yao Song with Ping pursued Sheng as far as Bamboo Ridge; Yao Zan led Longxi Grand Administrator Yao Qindu and Lüeyang Grand Administrator Wang Huan with household troops to hurry there.
proposals.after: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.
proposals.reason: 及 means actually catching up with Sheng, and the two 太守 are governors of the named commanderies; 禁兵 are palace guards.

units.zh: 贊至清水，嵩為盛所敗，嵩及秦都、王煥皆戰死。
units.en: At Qingshui, Yao Zan learned Yao Song had been crushed—Song, Qindu, and Wang Huan all lay dead.
units.literal: When Zan reached Qingshui, Song was defeated by Sheng; Song and Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.

proposals.before: At Qingshui, Yao Zan learned Yao Song had been crushed—Song, Qindu, and Wang Huan all lay dead.
proposals.after: When Yao Zan reached Qingshui, Yang Sheng defeated Yao Song. Song, Yao Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.
proposals.reason: The text synchronizes Zan’s arrival and Sheng’s victory; it does not say Zan learned of an earlier event.

units.zh: 贊至秦州，退還仇池。
units.en: Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, then withdrew to Chouqi.
units.literal: Zan reached Qinzhou and withdrew to Chouqi.

proposals.before: Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, then withdrew to Chouqi.
proposals.after: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.
proposals.reason: The chapter’s received-text collation identifies missing 盛 before 退還. Chouchi was the domain of Yang Sheng, whose invasion Zan came to relieve (s0055–58). See the Jinshu 119 校勘記, https://skqs.dazhishi.com/show_qmykvqkedv.html .

proposals.before: Zan reached Qinzhou and withdrew to Chouqi.
proposals.after: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.
proposals.reason: The chapter’s received-text collation identifies missing 盛 before 退還. Chouchi was the domain of Yang Sheng, whose invasion Zan came to relieve (s0055–58). See the Jinshu 119 校勘記, https://skqs.dazhishi.com/show_qmykvqkedv.html .

units.zh: 先是，天水冀縣石鼓鳴，聲聞數百里，野雉皆雊。
units.en: Earlier a stone drum in Jixian boomed for hundreds of li and pheasants called without cease.
units.literal: Before this, in Tianshui Jixian a stone drum sounded, heard for several hundred li, and wild pheasants all crowed.

proposals.before: Earlier a stone drum in Jixian boomed for hundreds of li and pheasants called without cease.
proposals.after: Earlier a stone drum had sounded in Ji county, Tianshui. It could be heard for several hundred li, and the wild pheasants all crowed.
proposals.reason: The drum was in Ji county of Tianshui, and 皆 means all the pheasants, not uninterrupted calling.

units.zh: 秦州地震者三十二，殷殷有聲者八，山崩舍壞，咸以為不祥。
units.en: Qinzhou then suffered dozens of quakes, rockslides, and ruined homes—everyone called it an ill omen.
units.literal: In Qinzhou there were thirty-two earthquakes with rumbling sound in eight cases; mountains collapsed and houses ruined—all thought it inauspicious.

proposals.before: Qinzhou then suffered dozens of quakes, rockslides, and ruined homes—everyone called it an ill omen.
proposals.after: Qinzhou suffered thirty-two earthquakes, eight accompanied by rumbling. Mountains collapsed and houses fell. Everyone took these as ill omens.
proposals.reason: Restore both numbers: thirty-two earthquakes and eight audible rumbles.

units.zh: 及嵩將出，群僚固諫止之。
units.en: When Yao Song prepared to march, the court begged him to stay.
units.literal: When Song was about to set out, the host of officials firmly remonstrated to stop him.

units.zh: 嵩曰：「若有不祥，此乃命也，安所逃乎！」
units.en: Yao Song said, "If doom comes, it is fate—there is no escape."
units.literal: Song said, "If there is inauspiciousness, this is fate—where would one flee!"

units.zh: 遂及於難。
units.en: He rode to his death.
units.literal: Thereupon he met disaster.

units.zh: 識者以為秦州泓之故鄉，將滅之征也。
units.en: Wise men said Qinzhou was Yao Hong's home ground—its ruin foretold his own.
units.literal: Those with insight thought Qinzhou was Hong's old homeland—an omen of its about to perish.

proposals.before: Wise men said Qinzhou was Yao Hong's home ground—its ruin foretold his own.
proposals.after: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.
proposals.reason: The omens concern Hong’s approaching fall because Qinzhou was his home region; the text does not report Qinzhou destroyed.

proposals.before: Those with insight thought Qinzhou was Hong's old homeland—an omen of its about to perish.
proposals.after: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.
proposals.reason: The omens concern Hong’s approaching fall because Qinzhou was his home region; the text does not report Qinzhou destroyed.

value.assessment: Qinzhou omens read as portent of Hong's coming ruin

units.zh: 赫連勃勃攻陷陰密，執秦州刺史姚軍都，坑將士五千餘人。
units.en: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, and slaughtered over five thousand troops.
units.literal: Helian Bobo attacked and took Yinmi, seized Qinzhou Inspector Yao Jundu, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and soldiers.

proposals.before: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, and slaughtered over five thousand troops.
proposals.after: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, inspector of Qinzhou, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and men.
proposals.reason: Recover Jundu’s office and the mass burial of the officers and soldiers.

units.zh: 軍都瞋目厲聲數勃勃殘忍之罪，不為之屈，勃勃怒而殺之。
units.en: Yao Jundu glared and cursed Bobo's cruelty to his face; Bobo slew him in rage.
units.literal: Jundu glared with eyes and in stern voice enumerated Bobo's crimes of cruelty and refused to yield to him; Bobo in anger killed him.

proposals.before: Yao Jundu glared and cursed Bobo's cruelty to his face; Bobo slew him in rage.
proposals.after: Yao Jundu glared at Bobo, loudly denounced his cruelty and refused to submit. Bobo killed him in a rage.
proposals.reason: 不為之屈 explicitly records his refusal to submit.

units.zh: 勃勃既克陰密，進兵侵雍，嶺北雜戶悉奔五將山。
units.en: After Yinmi, Bobo struck toward Yong and drove every northern household toward Five-General Mountain.
units.literal: Once Bobo had taken Yinmi, he advanced troops to invade Yong; north-of-the-ridge miscellaneous households all fled to Five-General Mountain.

proposals.before: After Yinmi, Bobo struck toward Yong and drove every northern household toward Five-General Mountain.
proposals.after: After taking Yinmi, Bobo advanced on Yong. The mixed households north of the ridge all fled to Five Generals Mountain.
proposals.reason: 嶺北雜戶 is the specific group of mixed households north of the ridge. They fled as Bobo invaded Yong.

units.zh: 征北姚恢棄安定，率戶五千奔新平，安定人胡儼、華韜等率眾距恢，恢單騎歸長安。
units.en: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao blocked him, and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
units.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui abandoned Anding, led five thousand households to flee to Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao led hosts to block Hui; Hui alone on horseback returned to Chang'an.

proposals.before: Yao Hui quit Anding with five thousand households for Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao blocked him, and he galloped alone back to Chang'an.
proposals.after: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, abandoned Anding and fled toward Xinping with five thousand households. Hu Yan, Hua Tao and others from Anding led their followers against him, and Hui returned to Chang’an alone on horseback.
proposals.reason: Restore Hui’s title and Yan and Tao leading followers in resistance.

units.zh: 立節彌姐成、建武裴岐為儼所殺，鎮西姚諶委鎮東走。
units.en: Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi died fighting Hu Yan; Yao Chen abandoned his post and ran east.
units.literal: Lijie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.

proposals.before: Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi died fighting Hu Yan; Yao Chen abandoned his post and ran east.
proposals.after: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.
proposals.reason: Yan killed the holders of two military titles; dying in battle is unspecified. Chen held the General Who Guards the West title.

proposals.before: Lijie Mijie Cheng and Jianwu Pei Qi were killed by Yan; General Who Guards the West Yao Chen abandoned the garrison and fled east.
proposals.after: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.
proposals.reason: Yan killed the holders of two military titles; dying in battle is unspecified. Chen held the General Who Guards the West title.

units.zh: 勃勃遂據雍，抄掠郿城。
units.en: Bobo then overran Yong and raided Mei.
units.literal: Bobo thereupon occupied Yong, raiding and plundering Mei city.

units.zh: 姚紹及征虜尹昭、鎮軍姚洽等率步騎五萬討勃勃，姚恢以精騎一萬繼之。
units.en: Yao Shao, Yin Zhao, and Yao Qia led fifty thousand men against Bobo; Yao Hui followed with ten thousand horse.
units.literal: Yao Shao and General Who Captures Barbarians Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia, and others led fifty thousand foot and horse to campaign against Bobo; Yao Hui with ten thousand picked cavalry followed them.

proposals.before: Yao Shao, Yin Zhao, and Yao Qia led fifty thousand men against Bobo; Yao Hui followed with ten thousand horse.
proposals.after: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.
proposals.reason: Restore two military titles, the mixed infantry and cavalry force, and the picked cavalry following them.

units.zh: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定，胡儼閉門距之，殺鮮卑數千人，據安定以降。
units.en: At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.
units.literal: The army halted at Hengshui; Bobo withdrew to guard Anding; Hu Yan closed the gate to block him, killed several thousand Xianbei, and occupied Anding to surrender.

proposals.before: At Hengshui Bobo pulled back to Anding; Hu Yan shut the gates, killed thousands of Xianbei, and handed the city over.
proposals.after: Shao’s army halted at Hengshui. Bobo fell back toward Anding to hold it, but Hu Yan shut the gates against him, killed several thousand Xianbei and surrendered the city.
proposals.reason: It is Shao’s army that camps at Hengshui. Bobo’s separate withdrawal was blocked at Anding.

units.zh: 紹進兵躡勃勃，戰於馬鞍阪，敗之，追至朝那，不及而還。
units.en: Yao Shao beat Bobo at Ma'an Ridge, chased him toward Zhaona, then broke off the pursuit.
units.literal: Shao advanced the army to tread on Bobo, fought at Ma'an Slope, defeated him, pursued to Zhaona, did not catch up and returned.

proposals.before: Yao Shao beat Bobo at Ma'an Ridge, chased him toward Zhaona, then broke off the pursuit.
proposals.after: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.
proposals.reason: The pursuit reached 朝那; Shao returned because he failed to catch Bobo.

proposals.before: Shao advanced the army to tread on Bobo, fought at Ma'an Slope, defeated him, pursued to Zhaona, did not catch up and returned.
proposals.after: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.
proposals.reason: The pursuit reached 朝那; Shao returned because he failed to catch Bobo.

units.zh: 楊盛遣兄子倦入寇長蛇。
units.en: Yang Sheng sent his nephew Yang Juan against Changshe.
units.literal: Yang Sheng sent his elder brother's son Juan to invade Changshe.

proposals.before: Yang Sheng sent his nephew Yang Juan against Changshe.
proposals.after: Yang Sheng sent Yang Juan, his elder brother’s son, to invade Changshe.
proposals.reason: 兄子 specifies the son of Sheng’s elder brother.

units.zh: 平陽氐苟渴聚眾千餘，據五丈原以叛，遣鎮遠姚萬、恢武姚難討之，為渴所敗。
units.en: The Di chief Gou Ke seized Wuzhangyuan; Yao Wan and Yao Nan marched against him and lost.
units.literal: Pingyang Di Gou Ke gathered more than a thousand, occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt; he sent General Who Guards the Distance Yao Wan and General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to campaign against him, and they were defeated by Ke.

proposals.before: The Di chief Gou Ke seized Wuzhangyuan; Yao Wan and Yao Nan marched against him and lost.
proposals.after: Gou Ke, a Di man of Pingyang, gathered more than a thousand men and occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt. Yao Hong sent Yao Wan, General Who Guards the Distant Lands, and Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, against him. Gou Ke defeated them.
proposals.reason: Restore Ke’s Pingyang affiliation, force of over a thousand, explicit rebellion and the two generals’ titles. No chieftaincy is stated.

units.zh: 姚諶討渴，擒之。
units.en: Yao Chen captured Gou Ke in a second expedition.
units.literal: Yao Chen campaigned against Ke and seized him.

units.zh: 泓使輔國斂曼嵬、前將軍姚光兒討楊倦于陳倉，倦奔于散關。
units.en: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Chencang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
units.literal: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Chencang; Juan fled to Sanguan.

proposals.before: Yao Hong sent Lian Mankui and Yao Guang'er to Chencang; Yang Juan bolted for Sanguan.
proposals.after: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.
proposals.reason: 嵬 is Wei in Manwei; both commanders have titles, and their mission was to attack Juan.

proposals.before: Hong sent General Who Supports the State Lian Mankui and Forward General Yao Guang'er to campaign against Yang Juan at Chencang; Juan fled to Sanguan.
proposals.after: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.
proposals.reason: 嵬 is Wei in Manwei; both commanders have titles, and their mission was to attack Juan.

units.zh: 勃勃遣兄子提南侵池陽，車騎姚裕、前將軍彭白狼、建義蛇玄距卻之。
units.en: Bobo's nephew Ti raided Chiyang but Yao Yu, Peng Bailang, and She Xuan threw him back.
units.literal: Bobo sent his elder brother's son Ti south to raid Chiyang; chariots and cavalry Yao Yu, Forward General Peng Bailang, and Jianyi She Xuan blocked him and drove him back.

proposals.before: Bobo's nephew Ti raided Chiyang but Yao Yu, Peng Bailang, and She Xuan threw him back.
proposals.after: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.
proposals.reason: Restore the elder brother’s son, the southward raid and all three officers’ roles; 車騎 denotes a general’s title.

proposals.before: Bobo sent his elder brother's son Ti south to raid Chiyang; chariots and cavalry Yao Yu, Forward General Peng Bailang, and Jianyi She Xuan blocked him and drove him back.
proposals.after: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.
proposals.reason: Restore the elder brother’s son, the southward raid and all three officers’ roles; 車騎 denotes a general’s title.

units.zh: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡入自淮、肥，攻漆丘、項城，將軍沈林子自汴入河，攻倉垣。
units.en: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.
units.literal: Before long Jin Grand Commandant Liu Yu commanded the great host to campaign against Hong, halted at Pengcheng, sent General Who Wins the Championship Tan Daoji and General Who Soars like Dragon Wang Zhen'e in from Huai and Fei to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng, General Shen Linzi from Bian into the He to attack Cangyuan.

proposals.before: Soon Liu Yu of Jin massed at Pengcheng and sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e through Huai-Fei against Qiqiu and Xiangcheng while Shen Linzi struck Cangyuan from Bian.
proposals.after: Soon afterward Jin’s grand commandant Liu Yu led a great army against Yao Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen’e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi entered the Yellow River from the Bian and attacked Cangyuan.
proposals.reason: Restore Liu Yu’s grand commandant office, his campaign against Hong, his officers’ military titles and Shen Linzi’s route from the Bian into the Yellow River.

units.zh: 泓將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，王師遂入潁口，所至多降服。
units.en: Wang Gousheng yielded Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e, Yao Zhang yielded Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji, and the Jin host poured through Yingkou almost unopposed.
units.literal: Hong's general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Zhen'e; Xuzhou Inspector Yao Zhang surrendered Xiangcheng to Daoji; the royal army then entered Yingkou, and wherever it went there was surrender.

proposals.before: Wang Gousheng yielded Qiqiu to Wang Zhen'e, Yao Zhang yielded Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji, and the Jin host poured through Yingkou almost unopposed.
proposals.after: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.
proposals.reason: 多 qualifies submissions: many places submitted. The first officer is Hong’s general and the second inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 惟新蔡太守董遵固守不降，道濟攻破之，縛遵而致諸軍門。
units.en: Only Dong Zun of Xin'cai held out until Tan Daoji stormed the city and bound him before the camp.
units.literal: Only Xin'cai Grand Administrator Dong Zun firmly guarded and would not surrender; Daoji broke him, bound Zun, and brought him to the army gate.

proposals.before: Only Dong Zun of Xin'cai held out until Tan Daoji stormed the city and bound him before the camp.
proposals.after: Only Dong Zun, governor of Xincai, held firm and refused to surrender. Tan Daoji stormed the place, had Zun bound and brought him to the gate of the camp.
proposals.reason: Restore Dong’s governorship and being brought bound to the camp gate.

units.zh: 遵厲色曰：「古之王者伐國，待士以禮。
units.en: Dong Zun snapped: "Ancient kings campaigned with courtesy toward worthy foes.
units.literal: Zun in stern color said, "Kings of old in campaigning against states treated knights with ritual.

proposals.before: Dong Zun snapped: "Ancient kings campaigned with courtesy toward worthy foes.
proposals.after: With a stern expression Dong Zun said, “When kings of old made war on other states, they treated men of worth with courtesy.
proposals.reason: 士 means men of standing or worth here; neither enemies specifically nor knights as a military class.

units.zh: 君奈何以不義行師，待國土以非禮乎。」
units.en: How dare you wage an unjust war and dishonor a loyal governor?"
units.literal: How can you, sir, march with unrighteous conduct and treat a state's knights without ritual."

proposals.before: How dare you wage an unjust war and dishonor a loyal governor?"
proposals.after: How can you wage war unjustly and treat a man of distinction in another state with such discourtesy?”
proposals.reason: The sealed text’s 土 is at odds with 士 in a Jinshu witness and the preceding 待士以禮. units.zh: 姚紹聞王師之至，還長安，言於泓曰：「晉師已過許昌，豫州、安定孤遠，卒難救衛，宜遷諸鎮戶內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，足以橫行天下。
units.en: Yao Shao raced back to warn Yao Hong: "Jin is past Xuchang—Yuzhou and Anding are too far to save. Move frontier households into the capital for a hundred thousand veterans.
units.literal: When Yao Shao heard the royal army had arrived, he returned to Chang'an and said to Hong, "The Jin army has passed Xuchang; Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and far; in the end hard to rescue—it is fitting to move the garrison households inward to fill the capital region; you can obtain crack troops of one hundred thousand, enough to range across the realm.

proposals.before: Yao Shao raced back to warn Yao Hong: "Jin is past Xuchang—Yuzhou and Anding are too far to save. Move frontier households into the capital for a hundred thousand veterans.
proposals.after: When Yao Shao heard of the Jin army’s arrival, he returned to Chang’an and told Hong, “Jin has already passed Xuchang. Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and distant and would be hard to relieve in an emergency. Move the garrison households inward to strengthen the capital region. We could raise a hundred thousand picked troops, enough to go anywhere in the realm.
proposals.reason: Restore Chang’an, Shao’s reason for returning, the garrisons’ isolation, and the claim the resulting force could range across the realm.

units.zh: 假使二寇交侵，無深害也。
units.en: Even if Bobo and Jin strike together, a thick core can absorb the blow.
units.literal: Even if the two bandits jointly invade, there is no deep harm.

sourceDate.text: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓

value.assessment: called Jin and Bobo the two bandits

units.zh: 如其不爾，晉侵豫州，勃勃寇安定者，將若之何！
units.en: Otherwise Jin will chew Yuzhou while Bobo gnaws Anding—what then?
units.literal: If it is not so—Jin invading Yuzhou and Bobo raiding Anding—what is to be done!

units.zh: 事機已至，宜在速決。」
units.en: The hour demands a fast decision."
units.literal: The moment of affairs has arrived; it is fitting to decide with speed."

units.zh: 其左僕射梁喜曰：「齊公恢雄勇有威名，為嶺北所憚，鎮人已與勃勃深仇，理應守死無貳，勃勃終不能棄安定遠寇京畿。
units.en: Liang Xi argued: "Yao Hui terrifies the north; his garrisons hate Bobo and will die before yielding—Bobo cannot skip Anding to strike the core.
units.literal: His left vice-director Liang Xi said, "Duke of Qi Hui is fierce and brave and has an awesome name, feared north of the ridge; the garrison people already have deep hatred with Bobo, by principle ought to guard unto death without second mind—Bobo in the end cannot abandon Anding and raid the capital region far.

proposals.before: Liang Xi argued: "Yao Hui terrifies the north; his garrisons hate Bobo and will die before yielding—Bobo cannot skip Anding to strike the core.
proposals.after: Liang Xi, the left vice-director, said, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, is brave and has a formidable reputation. The people north of the ridge fear him. The garrison’s people already bear Bobo a deep grudge and should hold out to the death without wavering. Bobo cannot bypass Anding and raid the distant capital region.
proposals.reason: Restore Liang’s office, Hui’s ducal rank, martial reputation north of the ridge, and the residents’ own hostility and determination.

units.zh: 若無安定，虜馬必及於郿、雍。
units.en: Lose Anding and enemy horsemen will reach Mei and Yong.
units.literal: If there is no Anding, enemy horses will surely reach Mei and Yong.

units.zh: 今關中兵馬足距晉師，豈可未有憂危先自削損也。」
units.en: Guanzhong can still face Jin—why cripple yourself before the crisis?"
units.literal: Now Guanzhong troops and horses are enough to stop the Jin army—how can one, not yet having worry and peril, first wound oneself by cutting away!"

units.en: Yao Hong sided with Liang Xi.
